I sit down to sort it out, and I don’t know what to do first… and before I know it, the whole day is gone.\n\nDoctor: Have you been having trouble remembering recent things?\n\nPatient: Yes, I have. I miss returning calls, or I’ll find a bill still sitting under a stack of mail when I thought I had handled it. I’ve forgotten errands I told my daughter I would do. And with my husband’s appointments, more than once I realized too late that I never called to confirm one. It’s been happening a lot.\n\nDoctor: When you were a child, did you also have a lot of trouble staying organized?\n\nPatient: Yes, I did. I remember even in grade school my teachers would say I was bright, but careless. I’d forget books or homework, and they’d have to remind me to finish my seatwork before I could go outside. It was something that came up more than once.\n\nDoctor: As an adult, before these recent memory concerns, did you also have ongoing trouble staying organized in everyday life?\n\nPatient: Yes. It’s gotten worse lately, but I’ve always had trouble keeping everyday things organized. It’s clearer now in everyday things. I’ll miss returning calls, or I’ll find bills sitting under a stack of mail that I meant to take care of. I’ve forgotten errands I promised my daughter I’d do, and more than once I realized too late that I never confirmed one of my husband’s appointments. It’s been happening more than it used to.\n\nDoctor: Have there been times when your confusion or memory problems came on suddenly or got much worse during an illness or after a medical problem?\n\nPatient: I’m not sure. I can’t think of a time where it suddenly came on because I was sick or after some medical problem. It feels more like it’s just been there and gotten worse over time.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever get lost in places that used to be familiar to you?\n\nPatient: I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed getting lost in places I know.
